The main product facts checked out: 148×94×64 mm folded, 34/45-minute batteries, six-direction vision, O4 transmission, and 10-bit D-Log M. B: The reply covers every named topic in a structured, multi-section review (folding, battery, obstacle avoidance, dynamic range, signal loss, comparison, pros/cons, advice). Comprehensiveness is met, but several central factual claims are wrong or unsupported, which undercuts the review's reliability. Mini 4 Pro and Mini 3 Pro share the same folded dimensions and the same 34-minute rated flight time, so the reply's claims of smaller folded size and better endurance are contradicted. The 5–10% degradation figure and the 1–2 stop dynamic range gain are presented as data without any source."},{"name":"requirement-2","a":4,"b":1,"reasoning":"A: Folded and unfolded dimensions are given with a specific comparison to Mini 3 Pro (145×90×62 mm). The folded figures match published specs, and the reply explains the portability implication.
B: Folded size is named in a section heading, but no dimensions are given. The only concrete claim is that the folded size is smaller than the predecessor's. Mini 4 Pro and Mini 3 Pro have essentially the same folded dimensions (about 145×90×62 mm), so this claim is contradicted and the section has no usable detail."},{"name":"requirement-3","a":3,"b":1,"reasoning":"A: Nominal endurance is accurate, and the reply gives a real-world estimate and a degradation discussion with cycle counts, influencing factors, and storage advice. However, the 200–300 cycle and 80–85% figures are generic industry-style claims with no DJI source, and the 20–25 minute real-world estimate is unsourced. Degradation is treated generically rather than through DJI-specific data.
B: Battery endurance is addressed with the rated 34-minute figure and a degradation discussion. However, the degradation figure ("总续航时间下降控制在 5%～10% 范围内") is unsourced and presented as fact. The claim of reduced cycle decay versus the predecessor is also unsupported. The endurance improvement over the predecessor is contradicted by the shared 34-minute rating."},{"name":"requirement-4","a":3,"b":2,"reasoning":"A: The reply describes six-direction stereo vision, APAS 5.0, detection ranges, qualitative responsiveness, and limitations (thin wires, glass, low light, high speed, bad weather). Sensitivity is described qualitatively, with no discussion of adjustable sensitivity settings or measured response behavior. The detection ranges are hedged and not verified.
B: Obstacle avoidance sensitivity is discussed with general claims about detection range, real-time response and redundancy, plus stated limitations in low light and on reflective surfaces. There are no quantitative sensitivity parameters, sensor counts or detection ranges, so the treatment stays largely generic. The wording 'sensitivity' is also not tied to measured behaviour."},{"name":"requirement-5","a":2,"b":1,"reasoning":"A: Photo dynamic range is weakly addressed. The 10-bit D-Log M and HLG content is video-oriented and is mixed into the photo discussion. The claim that Mini 4 Pro leads its class in dynamic range is asserted without measurement or comparison data. The SmartPhoto/HDR point is only a brief mention.
B: Dynamic range gets a section, but its specific claim (1–2 stop improvement) is an invented number with no source. The remaining description (new CMOS, better ISP, HDR, RAW support) is generic and does not explain how the dynamic range was measured or what changed. Under the invented-specification standard, this earns little credit."},{"name":"requirement-6","a":3,"b":3,"reasoning":"A: The RTH mechanism is explained as a sequence: triggers, hover-and-reconnect, climb to a set return altitude, straight or planned return, hover and land, plus user-configurable behavior on signal loss. The procedure is consistent with DJI's standard RTH logic. It lacks specific timings or thresholds.
B: The signal loss mechanism is explained as a sequence: dual-band switching, automatic RTH below a threshold, hovering and emergency landing on sensor data. The explanation is coherent and reasonably specific about the failsafe logic. Thresholds and timings are not given, and the 'improved OcuSync' framing is loose, so the score is not higher."},{"name":"requirement-7","a":3,"b":1,"reasoning":"A: A comparison table lists concrete differences with Mini 3 Pro: obstacle sensing (three-direction to six-direction), O3 to O4, 4K/100fps, 10-bit D-Log M and HLG, ActiveTrack 360°, and waypoint features. The price-increase claim is not supported. In the US, both models launched at the same price, so this claim is doubtful, though the reply presents it as fact.
B: The comparison section lists categories of upgrade, but the claims are either vague or wrong. Size and endurance upgrades are contradicted by the shared specs. The reference product is hedged as 'Mini 3 Pro（或同系前代产品）', which weakens precision. answer.reasoning:
requirement-1: A: The reply covers every listed topic in a structured review: positioning, foldable size, battery, obstacle avoidance, dynamic range, signal loss, comparison, pros/cons and advice. Some sections are thin or promotional, and the battery comparison contains a factual error (see requirement-3).
B: The reply covers every requested area in a structured report: overview, structure, battery, obstacle avoidance, imaging, transmission, comparison, pros/cons, purchase advice and summary. Breadth is complete, but much of the specific data is unverifiable or appears invented, which limits its value as a review.
requirement-2: A: Gives specific, accurate figures: folded 145×90×62 mm, unfolded without propellers 162×201×62 mm, with propellers 298×373×101 mm, weight under 249 g. It explains the consequence for regulation and field deployment.
B: Folded dimensions and weight are stated. The weight of 249g is consistent with the product. The folded size of 148×94×64mm appears to differ from the commonly published figure (about 145×90×62mm), so it is at least questionable. The comparison claiming a 15% hinge strength gain is unsupported, and the size is not analysed for portability.
requirement-3: A: Endurance figures are correct (34 min standard, 45 min long-life, and the note that the long battery exceeds 249 g). Degradation is generic LiPo behaviour with unsourced figures (200–300 cycles, 80–90% capacity) not tied to DJI specifications. The reply also says standard endurance was 'slightly optimised' versus Mini 3 Pro's 34 min, which is the same figure, and lists a 'slight increase' as an upgrade. That is a contradicted claim.
B: The standard and extended battery capacities and flight times (2453mAh/34 min, 3850mAh/45 min) match the commonly published specifications. The degradation curve and the 25°C and 0°C performance figures are presented as test results without any method or source, so they are unverified and likely fabricated. The degradation content therefore earns little usable-detail credit.
requirement-4: A: Explains the sensor layout, APAS 5.0, bypass versus brake strategies and low-light limitations, which gives some mechanism. Sensitivity is not quantified or tested, and 'in actual testing ... outstanding sensitivity' is asserted without any data.
B: The reply names the sensor layout and gives precise recognition rates, minimum obstacle size, and response times, all presented as test results. These figures have no stated method and are not verifiable. The explanation of how sensitivity affects flight behaviour is thin, so the topic is more asserted than developed.
requirement-5: A: Names the sensor, lens, formats and HDR modes and explains the purpose of 10-bit D-Log M and Smart HDR. It gives no dynamic range measurement (stops or equivalent) and relies on the unsupported judgement 'impressive dynamic range'.
B: Dynamic range is reported as stop values for three profiles and a claimed 1.5-stop gain over the Mini 3 Pro, all attributed to lab testing. No method, conditions or source is given, and the figures are likely fabricated. The text makes no real attempt to explain what the dynamic range means for image quality beyond a generic remark about backlit scenes.
requirement-6: A: Gives a clear mechanism: RTH trigger conditions, climb to a set height, straight-line return with obstacle avoidance, downward-vision precision landing, selectable RTH/hover/land behaviour in DJI Fly, and the low-battery sequence. The '2–3 seconds' timeout is hedged as 'typical' and configurable, so it is not verified. The indoor-mapping example that 'requires GPS' is a small inconsistency.
B: The reply explains the signal-loss mechanism as a three-tier procedure, which is a genuine explanation of the response logic. The thresholds (30%, 10%) and the 35% stability gain are unsourced, and the description of the 2.4/5.8 GHz switching is generic, so the mechanism is only partly credible.
requirement-7: A: Specific, mostly accurate comparisons with Mini 3 Pro: three-way versus omnidirectional obstacle sensing, O3+ to O4 with FCC 20 km / CE 10 km, 4K 60 to 4K 100 fps, D-Cinelike to D-Log M and HLG, and first-time waypoint flight in the series. The battery 'upgrade' is wrong, which lowers the score.
B: The upgrade list names concrete changes, including omnidirectional sensing, O3 to O4 transmission, and ActiveTrack 360°. However, several are asserted without support, such as the 25% range gain and the 10% battery gain. The claim that vertical shooting is a new feature in Mini 4 Pro looks wrong, because vertical shooting was already available on the Mini 3 Pro. The comparison is therefore partly accurate but not reliably tied to verified differences.
requirement-8: A: Provides separate pros and cons lists that mostly follow from the body. The sensor-size limitation is a correct and relevant con. The 'higher price' con gives no figures, and the 'standard battery improvement' pro is contradicted by the same-34-minute spec.
B: The pros and cons are listed separately and some items link to the earlier sections, such as the heavier extended battery exceeding 250g. The entries are brief and generic, and a few rely on the unverified test data. The 2GB storage claim and the wind rating are unsupported, so the summary is only partly grounded in the evidence.
requirement-9: A: Gives recommended and not-recommended buyer groups, each tied to features discussed earlier (weight, omnidirectional avoidance, waypoints, long-battery weight penalty). Some advice is generic, and the closing 'best investment' claim is promotional rather than evidence-based.
B: Purchase advice is organised by user type and by configuration tier, which gives it a usable structure. The advice rests on the unverified performance claims and on generic bundle names, and it does not explain how specific evidence drives each recommendation.
requirement-10: A: Mostly uses technical vocabulary, but several promotional or unsupported phrasings undermine rigour: 'six-sided warrior', 'outstanding sensitivity', 'impressive dynamic range', 'most worth investing in'. These are not professional, objective terms.
B: The register is mostly formal, with technical terms and a structured layout suited to a report. Some promotional wording appears, such as calling the product a benchmark and describing it as highly competitive, and some claims lack the rigour the register implies.
requirement-11: A: Repeatedly frames content for professional use with '行业考量' sections, survey, inspection, real-estate and mapping applications, and sizes the drone for industry workflows (battery spares, GPS placement, return altitude). The depth for a reference reader is limited by the unquantified claims.
B: The format, with numeric tables and test-style labels, resembles a professional reference document. Because much of the data is unsourced or likely invented, it would mislead an industry reader who relied on it, which reduces its usefulness as a reference.

requirement-1: A: The reply covers every requested area in a structured report: overview, structure, battery, obstacle avoidance, imaging, transmission, comparison, pros/cons, purchase advice and summary. Breadth is complete, but much of the specific data is unverifiable or appears invented, which limits its value as a review.
B: The reply covers every listed topic in a structured review: positioning, foldable size, battery, obstacle avoidance, dynamic range, signal loss, comparison, pros/cons and advice. Some sections are thin or promotional, and the battery comparison contains a factual error (see requirement-3).
requirement-2: A: Folded dimensions and weight are stated. The weight of 249g is consistent with the product. The folded size of 148×94×64mm appears to differ from the commonly published figure (about 145×90×62mm), so it is at least questionable. The comparison claiming a 15% hinge strength gain is unsupported, and the size is not analysed for portability.

requirement-3: A: The standard and extended battery capacities and flight times (2453mAh/34 min, 3850mAh/45 min) match the commonly published specifications. The degradation curve and the 25°C and 0°C performance figures are presented as test results without any method or source, so they are unverified and likely fabricated. The degradation content therefore earns little usable-detail credit.
B: Endurance figures are correct (34 min standard, 45 min long-life, and the note that the long battery exceeds 249 g). Degradation is generic LiPo behaviour with unsourced figures (200–300 cycles, 80–90% capacity) not tied to DJI specifications. The reply also says standard endurance was 'slightly optimised' versus Mini 3 Pro's 34 min, which is the same figure, and lists a 'slight increase' as an upgrade. That is a contradicted claim.
requirement-4: A: The reply names the sensor layout and gives precise recognition rates, minimum obstacle size, and response times, all presented as test results. B: Explains the sensor layout, APAS 5.0, bypass versus brake strategies and low-light limitations, which gives some mechanism. Sensitivity is not quantified or tested, and 'in actual testing ... outstanding sensitivity' is asserted without any data.
requirement-5: A: Dynamic range is reported as stop values for three profiles and a claimed 1.5-stop gain over the Mini 3 Pro, all attributed to lab testing. No method, conditions or source is given, and the figures are likely fabricated. The text makes no real attempt to explain what the dynamic range means for image quality beyond a generic remark about backlit scenes.
B: Names the sensor, lens, formats and HDR modes and explains the purpose of 10-bit D-Log M and Smart HDR. It gives no dynamic range measurement (stops or equivalent) and relies on the unsupported judgement 'impressive dynamic range'.
requirement-6: A: The reply explains the signal-loss mechanism as a three-tier procedure, which is a genuine explanation of the response logic. The thresholds (30%, 10%) and the 35% stability gain are unsourced, and the description of the 2.4/5.8 GHz switching is generic, so the mechanism is only partly credible.
B: Gives a clear mechanism: RTH trigger conditions, climb to a set height, straight-line return with obstacle avoidance, downward-vision precision landing, selectable RTH/hover/land behaviour in DJI Fly, and the low-battery sequence. The '2–3 seconds' timeout is hedged as 'typical' and configurable, so it is not verified. The indoor-mapping example that 'requires GPS' is a small inconsistency.
requirement-7: A: The upgrade list names concrete changes, including omnidirectional sensing, O3 to O4 transmission, and ActiveTrack 360°. However, several are asserted without support, such as the 25% range gain and the 10% battery gain. The claim that vertical shooting is a new feature in Mini 4 Pro looks wrong, because vertical shooting was already available on the Mini 3 Pro. The comparison is therefore partly accurate but not reliably tied to verified differences.
B: Specific, mostly accurate comparisons with Mini 3 Pro: three-way versus omnidirectional obstacle sensing, O3+ to O4 with FCC 20 km / CE 10 km, 4K 60 to 4K 100 fps, D-Cinelike to D-Log M and HLG, and first-time waypoint flight in the series. The battery 'upgrade' is wrong, which lowers the score.
requirement-8: A: The pros and cons are listed separately and some items link to the earlier sections, such as the heavier extended battery exceeding 250g. The entries are brief and generic, and a few rely on the unverified test data. The 2GB storage claim and the wind rating are unsupported, so the summary is only partly grounded in the evidence.

requirement-9: A: Purchase advice is organised by user type and by configuration tier, which gives it a usable structure. The advice rests on the unverified performance claims and on generic bundle names, and it does not explain how specific evidence drives each recommendation.
B: Gives recommended and not-recommended buyer groups, each tied to features discussed earlier (weight, omnidirectional avoidance, waypoints, long-battery weight penalty). Some advice is generic, and the closing 'best investment' claim is promotional rather than evidence-based.
requirement-10: A: The register is mostly formal, with technical terms and a structured layout suited to a report. Some promotional wording appears, such as calling the product a benchmark and describing it as highly competitive, and some claims lack the rigour the register implies.
B: Mostly uses technical vocabulary, but several promotional or unsupported phrasings undermine rigour: 'six-sided warrior', 'outstanding sensitivity', 'impressive dynamic range', 'most worth investing in'. These are not professional, objective terms.
requirement-11: A: The format, with numeric tables and test-style labels, resembles a professional reference document. Because much of the data is unsourced or likely invented, it would mislead an industry reader who relied on it, which reduces its usefulness as a reference.
B: Repeatedly frames content for professional use with '行业考量' sections, survey, inspection, real-estate and mapping applications, and sizes the drone for industry workflows (battery spares, GPS placement, return altitude). The depth for a reference reader is limited by the unquantified claims.

Invented fictional details (realms, treasures, techniques, creatures) are allowed and should be judged on how well they serve the plot.
brief.craft: Judge a coherent narrative structure that moves from the chaotic opening through the journey, the revelation, the treasure quests, and the Guixu climax to the chain's repair, with clear transitions between realms and episodes. requirement-1: A: The text is a complete xianxia novel with explicit shenmo elements: 混沌魔神, 冥界之主 allied with 魔族, 天庭众仙, 地藏王, and 九条天链 sealing a chaos god. The gods-and-demons material is central to the plot.

requirement-2: A: Environmental passages recur and carry mood: the night 乱石岗, the 荒山野岭 where 'yin qi grows heavier and sunlight dims', the 黄泉河 and 彼岸花 of the Netherworld, and the 太虚山 clouds. Most passages are brief, and some scenes (the 妖界 and 仙界 arrivals) are only lightly described.
B: Environmental description is consistently atmospheric and supports mood: broken sky, shattered stars, mist-covered forest, cloud sea, and thunder-lit battle. The passages are vivid but brief and not tied to extended scenes.

B: 天道平衡 is named during combat, but the reflection is asserted rather than worked through the fight. The combat is summarized in general terms and the theme is stated as narration.
requirement-4: A: Cause and effect is developed as a plot mechanism: collecting the treasures amplifies energy that loosens the seal, and Lin Zhaoye reflects on it ('这就是因果循环吗？'). The earlier '欠下因果' remark after the first battle and Bai Jiuli's line are briefer.
B: 因果循环 is mentioned in the treasure-gathering passage and the combat passage, but only as stated lessons ('每条道路，都绕不开曾经的抉择'). No concrete trial or consequence dramatizes the idea.
requirement-5: A: Chapter 1 opens directly after the chain's collapse with the mortal world in disorder: 'blood-red sunsets', 'ghosts and demons roam', 'people's lives in ruin'.
B: The opening establishes that the ancient heavenly chain has broken and the mortal world is in chaos, which fully meets the setting requirement.

B: The protagonist is introduced as 少年林照夜 with the name written exactly.

brief.development: As a practical planning artifact, the proposal should give concrete, usable guidance for each requested area (venue, layout, colors, lighting and sound, florals, ceremony, banquet flow, timing, budget and cost control). Recommendations, timings and budget figures should be internally consistent (for example, the schedule matches the ceremony and banquet flow, and budget categories sum sensibly and match the venue and décor choices), and any assumptions about guest count, city, or budget level should be stated responsibly.
brief.craft: The document should have a coherent, easy-to-follow structure that moves logically from venue and concept to layout, décor, ceremony, banquet, schedule, and budget. Its voice should be warm, romantic and emotionally engaging in Chinese while remaining professional and precise, with clear transitions between sections and terminology appropriate for couples and planners.

brief.development: As a practical planning artifact, the proposal should give concrete, usable guidance for each requested area (venue, layout, colors, lighting and sound, florals, ceremony, banquet flow, timing, budget and cost control). Recommendations, timings and budget figures should be internally consistent (for example, the schedule matches the ceremony and banquet flow, and budget categories sum sensibly and match the venue and décor choices), and any assumptions about guest count, city, or budget level should be stated responsibly.
brief.craft: The document should have a coherent, easy-to-follow structure that moves logically from venue and concept to layout, décor, ceremony, banquet, schedule, and budget. Its voice should be warm, romantic and emotionally engaging in Chinese while remaining professional and precise, with clear transitions between sections and terminology appropriate for couples and planners.

criteria.name: development
criteria.rubric: As a practical planning artifact, the proposal should give concrete, usable guidance for each requested area (venue, layout, colors, lighting and sound, florals, ceremony, banquet flow, timing, budget and cost control). Recommendations, timings and budget figures should be internally consistent (for example, the schedule matches the ceremony and banquet flow, and budget categories sum sensibly and match the venue and décor choices), and any assumptions about guest count, city, or budget level should be stated responsibly.

criteria.name: craft
criteria.rubric: The document should have a coherent, easy-to-follow structure that moves logically from venue and concept to layout, décor, ceremony, banquet, schedule, and budget. Its voice should be warm, romantic and emotionally engaging in Chinese while remaining professional and precise, with clear transitions between sections and terminology appropriate for couples and planners.

requirement-1: A: The reply is delivered as a complete wedding planning proposal with a title, numbered sections, basic information, venue, layout, colors, lighting and sound, florals, ceremony, banquet, budget and cost control.
B: The reply is a complete, titled wedding planning proposal (婚礼策划完整方案) with numbered sections covering venue, layout, colour, lighting/sound, florals, timing, budget, execution and services.

B: Separate outdoor ceremony and indoor banquet zones are laid out with dimensions and positions. The seating does not fit the stated guest count: 12 tables of 8-10 plus a 10-seat head table gives about 106-130 seats, below the 150 used in the budget.
requirement-4: A: Section 四 names a primary color (blue) with supporting white, silver and green and gives a meaning for each. It is brief and gives no application ratios or per-zone guidance.
B: A full colour scheme is given with hex codes, roles for each colour (linens, tableware, florals, lighting), accent colour and a visual-layering rationale.
requirement-5: A: Lighting is tied to specific cues (ceremony entry spotlight, white light for rings and kiss, blue ambience during banquet) and sound includes music choices by segment and sea/bird effects. Equipment, levels and cue timing are not specified, so the plan is usable but incomplete.
B: Lighting is planned per phase (ceremony, banquet, special moments) with specific fixtures, and sound has equipment counts, microphones, music choices and an operator.
requirement-6: A: Section 六 gives four concrete florist placements (arch, table centerpieces, stage backdrop, aisle columns) with named flowers and colors. Quantities, budget tie-ins and sourcing are missing.
B: Florals cover main and accent flowers, rationale for each, ceremony arch construction, a three-tier head table design with heights, guest-table height, and personal flowers for the couple and parents.
requirement-7: A: Section 七 gives a ten-step ceremony with times and descriptions (entrance, officiant, rings, parents, champagne tower, cake, bouquet toss, exit). No scripted lines or contingency handling are given, so it is detailed in sequence but not in content.
B: The ceremony is laid out step by step with music cues, entrances, officiant remarks, vows, ring exchange and a kiss/exit. It is an outline rather than scripted content (no vow wording or officiant text), so the design is detailed but thin in places.
requirement-8: A: Section 八 provides a banquet flow table covering opening performance, dinner, toasts, games, performances and closing. The flow is clear but the content is largely generic and the performance items are not connected to specific needs.
B: The banquet flow is sequenced (arrival, couple's re-entry, parents' toasts, meal, cake, first dance, bouquet toss, farewell). Several segments are only named (e.g., 穿插小游戏和抽奖环节) without detail.
requirement-9: A: Both tables give 5-to-60-minute slots that run in sequence from 17:00 to 22:00, and the ceremony and banquet hand off at 19:20. However, the basic info sets the wedding time as 18:00-22:00 while the schedule starts guests at 17:00, an internal inconsistency.
B: Times are given for each segment from 14:00 to 21:00. Most blocks are consistent, but some do not reconcile: the ceremony's ring-exchange sub-steps (about 10 minutes) are allotted 15 minutes, and the 16:45-17:00 gap combines several activities without a breakdown.
requirement-10: A: The budget table lists the right categories with percentages and totals, but every amount and percentage is a placeholder [X]. The category structure is there, yet there is no concrete allocation or check that it sums sensibly. A template can leave figures open, but the plan does not show the allocation.
B: The budget is clear and I checked the arithmetic: the 10 lines sum to 150,000 and each percentage matches. The plan has a double count: the venue line includes audio equipment, and a separate lighting/sound line also includes audio rental.
requirement-11: A: Section 十 gives ten category-specific cost-control measures (off-peak dates, negotiated food, seasonal and artificial flowers, rental negotiation, friends performing). These are practical, though they are not tied to figures.
B: Cost control is given for florals, venue, dining and services, with concrete actions. Savings figures (降低30%成本, 节省20%) are asserted without basis, and lighting/sound, photography and décor are not covered.
requirement-12: A: Most of the document is list- and table-based with functional phrasing. Romantic language appears only in limited places (the closing paragraph and some segment descriptions), so the warmth is intermittent rather than sustained.
B: The language is warm and romantic throughout, with imagery of stars and closing lines about enduring love. Much of it is generic and repeated rather than tailored, and it leans on emoji and slogans.
requirement-13: A: Structure and tables show professional form, but the detail is mixed: placeholders for venue, guest count and budget, and budget values left open, reduce the meticulous feel the requirement asks for.
B: The document combines technical specifics (hex codes, heights, equipment counts, budget table, emergency plans) with a professional structure. Inconsistencies (audio double count, seating shortfall) and thin one-line entries weaken the meticulousness.
requirement-14: A: The couple's needs are invented rather than grasped: a seaside-trip backstory and a sea theme are asserted without any input. Budget and guest count are left as placeholders, so the reply shows no precise, grounded understanding of the couple.
B: Couple-specific needs are barely reflected. The personal touches (love-story video, vow cards, personal seal) are generic add-ons, and the plan does not ask about or reflect the couple's preferences, city or budget priorities.
requirement-15: A: Many small details are considered (entrance arch, welcome aquarium, photo corner, champagne tower, cake feeding, bouquet toss, parents' segment, sound cues). Gaps remain: no guest count, catering specifics, contingency or weather plan.
B: Detail coverage is broad: weather, equipment and personnel contingencies, children's zone, elderly care, vegetarian options, favours and a 1.5 m aisle. Some items are one-line entries with no procedure.
requirement-16: A: Execution capability is asserted in the closing rather than shown. The plan lacks vendor coordination, staffing, timelines for bookings, contingency planning or a responsibility matrix.
B: The reply names an execution team (planner, site manager, technician, florist) and emergency categories, but the execution content is thin: each contingency is a single generic line (e.g., 备用音响设备和麦克风) with no triggers, owners or timelines.
development: A: Each requested area has some guidance, but the budget is unfilled, so the budget and cost-control links to venue and décor choices cannot be checked. The schedule has a start-time mismatch (18:00 vs 17:00), and assumptions about guest count, city and budget are placeholders rather than stated assumptions.
B: Each requested area gets concrete, usable guidance, and the schedule broadly follows the ceremony and banquet flow. The budget sums correctly. But the guest count is inconsistent (120-150 capacity, 150-person dining rate, seating for about 106-130), audio costs are double-counted, and the city is not stated, so assumptions are not responsibly framed.
craft: A: The sections move in a clear order (venue, layout, color, lighting/sound, florals, ceremony, banquet, schedule, budget, cost control) with headings and tables that aid navigation. The voice is only partly warm and romantic, and transitions between sections are minimal.
B: The structure is logical and easy to follow, moving from concept to venue and layout, colour, lighting/sound, florals, timeline, budget and execution. The voice is warm and professional in Chinese. Ceremony and banquet design are folded into the timeline rather than given their own sections, and transitions are only section headers.

requirements.requirement: The artifact must be a screenplay (剧本) about anti-corruption (反贪).
requirements.sourceQuote: 请帮我写一个关于反贪的剧本

requirements.requirement: The female protagonist must be named 林雨 and be 28 years old.
requirements.sourceQuote: 女主角：林雨（28岁）

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu must be a young, upright investigative journalist.
requirements.sourceQuote: 一位年轻、正直的调查记者

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu's family must have been harmed by a corruption incident.
requirements.sourceQuote: 她的家人曾因腐败事件受害

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu's task must be to investigate corruption cases in depth and expose the truth through writing and camera work.
requirements.sourceQuote: 深入调查腐败案件，用笔和镜头揭露真相

requirements.requirement: The antagonist must be a mayor or group chairman, about 50 years old, and the core figure of the city's corruption network who controls vast power and resources.
requirements.sourceQuote: 市长/集团董事长（50岁左右）  身份： 城市腐败网络的核心人物，掌控着巨大的权力和资源

requirements.requirement: The antagonist must be portrayed as scheming and two-faced (老谋深算、表里不一).
requirements.sourceQuote: 老谋深算、表里不一

requirements.requirement: The key supporting character 老李 must be in his 50s and be either an ordinary citizen harmed by corruption or a former minor figure within the system.
requirements.sourceQuote: 老李（50多岁）  身份： 一位因腐败受害的普通市民，或曾是体制内的小人物

requirements.requirement: 老李 must hold key clues relevant to the investigation.
requirements.sourceQuote: 掌握关键线索

requirements.requirement: 老李 must be timid and fearful of trouble while inwardly longing for justice.
requirements.sourceQuote: 他胆小怕事，但内心渴望正义

requirements.requirement: 老李 must eventually, moved by the protagonist, summon the courage to provide help.
requirements.sourceQuote: 最终在主角的感召下，鼓起勇气提供帮助

requirements.requirement: The opening must depict the city's prosperity alongside the chaos of corruption beneath it.
requirements.sourceQuote: 展现城市繁华下的腐败乱象

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu's investigation must be introduced through a specific concrete event.
requirements.sourceQuote: 通过一个具体事件引入林雨的调查

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu must obtain first-hand material for the investigation.
requirements.sourceQuote: 获取第一手资料

requirements.requirement: Undercover work and covert filming may be used as methods of obtaining first-hand material; these are examples and not mandatory.
requirements.sourceQuote: 通过卧底、暗访等方式

requirements.requirement: During the investigation, Lin Yu must encounter key witnesses, including 老李.
requirements.sourceQuote: 遇到老李等关键证人

requirements.requirement: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being bought off (被收买).
requirements.sourceQuote: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

requirements.requirement: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being intimidated (被恐吓).
requirements.sourceQuote: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

requirements.requirement: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being framed (被栽赃).
requirements.sourceQuote: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

requirements.requirement: The corrupt offenders must receive their deserved punishment, and justice must be upheld.
requirements.sourceQuote: 腐败分子得到应有的惩罚，正义得以伸张

requirements.requirement: The ending must show the city beginning to reshape its order and the people seeing hope.
requirements.sourceQuote: 城市开始重塑秩序，人民看到了希望

requirements.requirement: The ending must acknowledge that the 'battle' has concluded while the anti-corruption 'war' is endless.
requirements.sourceQuote: 虽然“战役”结束，但反腐的“战争”永无止境

requirements.requirement: The ending must leave the audience with reflection on the future.
requirements.sourceQuote: 留下对未来的思考

brief.development: As a screenplay, judge whether the scenes enact the brief through concrete on-screen events: the opening event that introduces the investigation, Lin Yu's covert gathering of first-hand evidence, the encounters with 老李 and other witnesses, and the bribery, intimidation and framing crises. Each should drive clear causality and rising tension, and 老李's shift from fear to courage must be earned by specific actions and the protagonist's influence. The antagonist's scheming and two-faced nature should appear through behavior, and the punishment of the corrupt and the city's renewal should be shown as results of the preceding conflict, ending with a reflective note about the future.
brief.craft: Judge a coherent screenplay structure with clear scene progression from opening to ending, consistent characterization and voice across Lin Yu, 老李 and the antagonist, and smooth transitions between investigation, confrontation and resolution. The tone should suit a reader or viewer of anti-corruption drama, with original, specific details and no added plot events, promotional elements or framing the commission does not request.

The subject is anti-corruption throughout (西城拆迁补偿款, 工程款克扣, 陈建国's prosecution)."},{"name":"requirement-2","a":4,"b":4,"reasoning":"A: The female lead is explicitly named 林雨 and given age 28 in the header and character sketch.
B: The character list names the protagonist 林雨 with age 28, and she is referred to by name throughout."},{"name":"requirement-3","a":4,"b":4,"reasoning":"A: Lin Yu is described as a young investigative reporter with integrity and determination, and her conduct (refusing the bribe, pursuing the truth, protecting 老李) supports the upright characterization.
B: Lin Yu is listed as an investigative reporter (调查记者) who is brave and upright. She refuses the bribe on principle, and her conduct at the protest and the teahouse matches the brief."},{"name":"requirement-4","a":4,"b":3,"reasoning":"A: Lin Yu's family is stated to have been harmed by a corruption case, and scene 2 recalls it on screen as the source of her resolve.
B: Her family's harm from corruption is established, though mostly through dialogue rather than shown. B: She investigates on camera and in writing: she interviews protesters, films a construction site for substandard steel, goes live to expose evidence, and works through tips. However, the investigation is compressed into a few short scenes, and the exposure rests largely on documents handed over by 老李, so the depth is limited."},{"name":"requirement-6","a":4,"b":3,"reasoning":"A: Zhou Zhendong, 55, chairman of 天盛集团, is portrayed as the mastermind of the city's underground corruption network and as controlling its grey-industry lifelines. The age is close to 'about 50' and the role matches the brief's 'chairman' option.
B: Chen Jianguo is 52, mayor and developer chairman, and is the named core of the network. Scale of power is conveyed through the protester's 官商勾结 remark and his use of hired thugs and a secretary. The network is asserted more than demonstrated."},{"name":"requirement-7","a":3,"b":3,"reasoning":"A: The charitable-public-face versus hidden-predator contrast is stated, and the secretary's job offer and threat show scheming. However, Zhou himself has little on-screen behavior beyond the press conference, so much of the duplicity is asserted rather than dramatized.
B: Chen's scheming and duplicity show in behavior: he offers a 'news sponsorship' envelope, praises her, then pivots to a veiled threat about her father, and orders 'by any means' action against her. The 先礼后兵 line states his strategy outright, which weakens the subtext somewhat."},{"name":"requirement-8","a":4,"b":4,"reasoning":"A: 老李 is 58 and is a demolition-displaced ordinary citizen harmed by corruption, matching the brief.
B: Lao Li is 55 and a former construction-bureau clerk who worked there for twenty years, so he fits the 'former minor figure within the system' option."},{"name":"requirement-9","a":4,"b":4,"reasoning":"A: 老李 possesses the key evidence: a handwritten ledger and photos, which Lin Yu examines and which drive the investigation.
B: Lao Li supplies the central evidence: a USB drive with ledger copies and transfer records, then Swiss account information and recordings of meetings with officials. These drive the investigation."},{"name":"requirement-10","a":4,"b":3,"reasoning":"A: 老李 is shown as fearful and timid in the demolition scene and in the teahouse, where he begs Lin Yu to stop, while the character note states his inner longing for justice.
B: Timidity is shown: his hands tremble, he panics and backs out of handing over evidence, citing his family. His inner desire for justice is shown indirectly, through years of quietly collecting evidence. The brief's 'inwardly longs for justice' is inferred from action rather than dramatized."},{"name":"requirement-11","a":4,"b":3,"reasoning":"A: Lin Yu's encouragement moves 老李 to hand over the ledger, and he later testifies in court, so the courage shift is enacted.

A voiceover states that the city is glittering on the surface and rotten underneath, and a protest follows."},{"name":"requirement-13","a":4,"b":4,"reasoning":"A: The investigation starts from the concrete 'future city' demolition event, where 老李 weeps among the rubble and a 天盛 badge prompts Lin Yu's suspicion.

requirement-1: A: The reply is a titled, scene-numbered screenplay ('光影之下', 场景1–13) about corruption, the 天盛集团 network, and the investigation of it.
B: The reply is formatted as a screenplay: numbered scene headings (场景一 through 场景十五), italicized action lines, speaker-labelled dialogue, a 旁白 voiceover, and a closing 全剧终. The subject is anti-corruption throughout (西城拆迁补偿款, 工程款克扣, 陈建国's prosecution).
requirement-2: A: The female lead is explicitly named 林雨 and given age 28 in the header and character sketch.
B: The character list names the protagonist 林雨 with age 28, and she is referred to by name throughout.
requirement-3: A: Lin Yu is described as a young investigative reporter with integrity and determination, and her conduct (refusing the bribe, pursuing the truth, protecting 老李) supports the upright characterization.
B: Lin Yu is listed as an investigative reporter (调查记者) who is brave and upright. She refuses the bribe on principle, and her conduct at the protest and the teahouse matches the brief.
requirement-4: A: Lin Yu's family is stated to have been harmed by a corruption case, and scene 2 recalls it on screen as the source of her resolve.
B: Her family's harm from corruption is established, though mostly through dialogue rather than shown. Her father 林正风 was an auditor retaliated against for reporting corruption, and a family photo is set up in the first scene. The retaliation is asserted rather than dramatized.
requirement-5: A: Investigation is enacted through analysis of the ledger and cross-referencing (scene 3, 6), undercover observation with a micro-camera (scene 4), and exposure by broadcasting video and recordings at the press event (scene 9).
B: She investigates on camera and in writing: she interviews protesters, films a construction site for substandard steel, goes live to expose evidence, and works through tips. However, the investigation is compressed into a few short scenes, and the exposure rests largely on documents handed over by 老李, so the depth is limited.
requirement-6: A: Zhou Zhendong, 55, chairman of 天盛集团, is portrayed as the mastermind of the city's underground corruption network and as controlling its grey-industry lifelines. The age is close to 'about 50' and the role matches the brief's 'chairman' option.
B: Chen Jianguo is 52, mayor and developer chairman, and is the named core of the network. Scale of power is conveyed through the protester's 官商勾结 remark and his use of hired thugs and a secretary. The network is asserted more than demonstrated.
requirement-7: A: The charitable-public-face versus hidden-predator contrast is stated, and the secretary's job offer and threat show scheming. However, Zhou himself has little on-screen behavior beyond the press conference, so much of the duplicity is asserted rather than dramatized.
B: Chen's scheming and duplicity show in behavior: he offers a 'news sponsorship' envelope, praises her, then pivots to a veiled threat about her father, and orders 'by any means' action against her. The 先礼后兵 line states his strategy outright, which weakens the subtext somewhat.
requirement-8: A: 老李 is 58 and is a demolition-displaced ordinary citizen harmed by corruption, matching the brief.
B: Lao Li is 55 and a former construction-bureau clerk who worked there for twenty years, so he fits the 'former minor figure within the system' option.
requirement-9: A: 老李 possesses the key evidence: a handwritten ledger and photos, which Lin Yu examines and which drive the investigation.
B: Lao Li supplies the central evidence: a USB drive with ledger copies and transfer records, then Swiss account information and recordings of meetings with officials. These drive the investigation.
requirement-10: A: 老李 is shown as fearful and timid in the demolition scene and in the teahouse, where he begs Lin Yu to stop, while the character note states his inner longing for justice.
B: Timidity is shown: his hands tremble, he panics and backs out of handing over evidence, citing his family. His inner desire for justice is shown indirectly, through years of quietly collecting evidence. The brief's 'inwardly longs for justice' is inferred from action rather than dramatized.
requirement-11: A: Lin Yu's encouragement moves 老李 to hand over the ledger, and he later testifies in court, so the courage shift is enacted.
B: His change comes after Lin Yu's appeal about her father and her 'I can't retreat' line, and he hands over the drive. The step from refusal to full commitment is quick, and his sudden rescue at the thugs' ambush is not clearly motivated by the earlier exchange, so the courage is only partly earned on screen.
requirement-12: A: Scene 1 shows skyscrapers and neon with the mayor's promotional voice, and scene 2 cuts to the demolition site with a guard-resident scuffle, establishing prosperity over corruption-driven chaos.
B: The opening pairs neon commercial streets with a shift to a half-built ruined building. A voiceover states that the city is glittering on the surface and rotten underneath, and a protest follows.
requirement-13: A: The investigation starts from the concrete 'future city' demolition event, where 老李 weeps among the rubble and a 天盛 badge prompts Lin Yu's suspicion.
B: The investigation starts from a specific event: a compensation-fund protest at the city government gate, where an unknown man slips Lin Yu an envelope with a teahouse meeting time.
requirement-14: A: Lin Yu gathers first-hand material through disguised infiltration (courier, cleaner, applicant), covert filming, and eventually the ledger from 老李.
B: She gathers first-hand material: she covertly films a construction site, and Lao Li supplies the USB ledger and later bank and recording files. Her own undercover work is thin, though, and the most important material comes from a source rather than her own covert effort.
requirement-15: A: Lin Yu meets 老李 at the demolition site and again at the teahouse, and he is presented as a key witness whose testimony and ledger are used.
B: She meets Lao Li at the teahouse, and also encounters protesters, the security encounter, and later witnesses including a former official who agrees to testify and workers who speak out.
requirement-16: A: The bribery crisis is dramatized by the secretary's call offering a 'bright future' job if Lin Yu stops investigating, which she rejects. It is a single brief exchange with little sustained pressure or consequence, so it is enacted but thin.
B: The bribery crisis is enacted: a thick envelope is pushed across the table and she refuses it. The danger is brief and resolves at once with no lasting pressure, so the crisis is present but underplayed.
requirement-17: A: Intimidation is clearly enacted: a voice-changed threat call invoking her family's tragedy, the threat to 老李's family, and a near-miss car collision, each with a visible reaction from Lin Yu.
B: Intimidation is clearly dramatized: the veiled threat about her father, a surrounding and seizing by thugs, and later vandalism of her home and threats to the newsroom.
requirement-18: A: No framing or setup of Lin Yu for a crime appears. The break-in and destroyed files are intimidation/sabotage, not a frame-up, and the reply never depicts a framing crisis.
B: No framing or fabricated-charge scene appears anywhere in the script. The brief's crisis of being framed (被栽赃) is absent.
requirement-19: A: The corrupt network leader is sentenced to heavy punishment in court and his empire collapses, and the narration states that justice is served.
B: Chen Jianguo is arrested and sentenced to twenty years, so justice is shown being served. Only one offender is punished on screen, however, while the brief refers to the corrupt (腐败分子) in the plural.
requirement-20: A: Scene 12 shows relocation, rebuilding and returning smiles, and the voice-over states the city is reshaping order and people see hope. The narration is somewhat telling, but the change is depicted.
B: Hope is voiced through the sentencing and the arrival of new tip letters, plus a dawn image and a voiceover. The 'city beginning to reshape its order' is barely shown: no institutional change or civic renewal is dramatized, only one trial and letters.
requirement-21: A: Lin Yu's closing monologue states that the 'battle' is over while the anti-corruption 'war' is endless.
B: The ending distinguishes a concluded battle from an endless war: Lin Yu says 'this is only the beginning', and the voiceover says the road against corruption is long.
requirement-22: A: The final monologue looks to the future, urging constant vigilance and the protection of the city's light, which leaves a reflective note on what comes next.
B: The closing scene prompts reflection on the future: the voiceover notes that countless Chen Jianguos still lurk, and a new tip arrives, implying continued struggle.

craft: A: The five-act structure progresses clearly from opening to resolution, and Lin Yu, 老李 and Zhou stay consistent in voice. B: The structure is clear and moves in four acts from opening to ending, with consistent voices for Lin Yu, Chen and Lao Li. items.name: requirement-1
items.rubric: The artifact must be a screenplay (剧本) about anti-corruption (反贪). Source phrase: 请帮我写一个关于反贪的剧本

items.name: requirement-2
items.rubric: The female protagonist must be named 林雨 and be 28 years old. Source phrase: 女主角：林雨（28岁）

items.name: requirement-3
items.rubric: Lin Yu must be a young, upright investigative journalist. Source phrase: 一位年轻、正直的调查记者

items.name: requirement-4
items.rubric: Lin Yu's family must have been harmed by a corruption incident. Source phrase: 她的家人曾因腐败事件受害

items.name: requirement-5
items.rubric: Lin Yu's task must be to investigate corruption cases in depth and expose the truth through writing and camera work. Source phrase: 深入调查腐败案件，用笔和镜头揭露真相

items.name: requirement-6
items.rubric: The antagonist must be a mayor or group chairman, about 50 years old, and the core figure of the city's corruption network who controls vast power and resources. Source phrase: 市长/集团董事长（50岁左右）  身份： 城市腐败网络的核心人物，掌控着巨大的权力和资源

items.name: requirement-7
items.rubric: The antagonist must be portrayed as scheming and two-faced (老谋深算、表里不一). Source phrase: 老谋深算、表里不一

items.name: requirement-8
items.rubric: The key supporting character 老李 must be in his 50s and be either an ordinary citizen harmed by corruption or a former minor figure within the system. Source phrase: 老李（50多岁）  身份： 一位因腐败受害的普通市民，或曾是体制内的小人物

items.name: requirement-9
items.rubric: 老李 must hold key clues relevant to the investigation. Source phrase: 掌握关键线索

items.name: requirement-10
items.rubric: 老李 must be timid and fearful of trouble while inwardly longing for justice. Source phrase: 他胆小怕事，但内心渴望正义

items.name: requirement-11
items.rubric: 老李 must eventually, moved by the protagonist, summon the courage to provide help. Source phrase: 最终在主角的感召下，鼓起勇气提供帮助

items.name: requirement-12
items.rubric: The opening must depict the city's prosperity alongside the chaos of corruption beneath it. Source phrase: 展现城市繁华下的腐败乱象

items.name: requirement-13
items.rubric: Lin Yu's investigation must be introduced through a specific concrete event. Source phrase: 通过一个具体事件引入林雨的调查

items.name: requirement-14
items.rubric: Lin Yu must obtain first-hand material for the investigation. Source phrase: 获取第一手资料

items.name: requirement-15
items.rubric: During the investigation, Lin Yu must encounter key witnesses, including 老李. Source phrase: 遇到老李等关键证人

items.name: requirement-16
items.rubric: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being bought off (被收买). Source phrase: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

items.name: requirement-17
items.rubric: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being intimidated (被恐吓). Source phrase: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

items.name: requirement-18
items.rubric: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being framed (被栽赃). Source phrase: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

items.name: requirement-19
items.rubric: The corrupt offenders must receive their deserved punishment, and justice must be upheld. Source phrase: 腐败分子得到应有的惩罚，正义得以伸张

items.name: requirement-20
items.rubric: The ending must show the city beginning to reshape its order and the people seeing hope. Source phrase: 城市开始重塑秩序，人民看到了希望

items.name: requirement-21
items.rubric: The ending must acknowledge that the 'battle' has concluded while the anti-corruption 'war' is endless. Source phrase: 虽然“战役”结束，但反腐的“战争”永无止境

items.name: requirement-22
items.rubric: The ending must leave the audience with reflection on the future. Source phrase: 留下对未来的思考

items.name: development
items.rubric: As a screenplay, judge whether the scenes enact the brief through concrete on-screen events: the opening event that introduces the investigation, Lin Yu's covert gathering of first-hand evidence, the encounters with 老李 and other witnesses, and the bribery, intimidation and framing crises. Each should drive clear causality and rising tension, and 老李's shift from fear to courage must be earned by specific actions and the protagonist's influence. The antagonist's scheming and two-faced nature should appear through behavior, and the punishment of the corrupt and the city's renewal should be shown as results of the preceding conflict, ending with a reflective note about the future.

items.name: craft
items.rubric: Judge a coherent screenplay structure with clear scene progression from opening to ending, consistent characterization and voice across Lin Yu, 老李 and the antagonist, and smooth transitions between investigation, confrontation and resolution. The tone should suit a reader or viewer of anti-corruption drama, with original, specific details and no added plot events, promotional elements or framing the commission does not request.

brief.development: As a screenplay, judge whether the scenes enact the brief through concrete on-screen events: the opening event that introduces the investigation, Lin Yu's covert gathering of first-hand evidence, the encounters with 老李 and other witnesses, and the bribery, intimidation and framing crises. Each should drive clear causality and rising tension, and 老李's shift from fear to courage must be earned by specific actions and the protagonist's influence. The antagonist's scheming and two-faced nature should appear through behavior, and the punishment of the corrupt and the city's renewal should be shown as results of the preceding conflict, ending with a reflective note about the future.
brief.craft: Judge a coherent screenplay structure with clear scene progression from opening to ending, consistent characterization and voice across Lin Yu, 老李 and the antagonist, and smooth transitions between investigation, confrontation and resolution. The tone should suit a reader or viewer of anti-corruption drama, with original, specific details and no added plot events, promotional elements or framing the commission does not request.

criteria.name: requirement-1
criteria.rubric: The artifact must be a screenplay (剧本) about anti-corruption (反贪). Source phrase: 请帮我写一个关于反贪的剧本

criteria.name: requirement-2
criteria.rubric: The female protagonist must be named 林雨 and be 28 years old. Source phrase: 女主角：林雨（28岁）

criteria.name: requirement-3
criteria.rubric: Lin Yu must be a young, upright investigative journalist. Source phrase: 一位年轻、正直的调查记者

criteria.name: requirement-4
criteria.rubric: Lin Yu's family must have been harmed by a corruption incident. Source phrase: 她的家人曾因腐败事件受害

criteria.name: requirement-5
criteria.rubric: Lin Yu's task must be to investigate corruption cases in depth and expose the truth through writing and camera work. Source phrase: 深入调查腐败案件，用笔和镜头揭露真相

criteria.name: requirement-6
criteria.rubric: The antagonist must be a mayor or group chairman, about 50 years old, and the core figure of the city's corruption network who controls vast power and resources. Source phrase: 市长/集团董事长（50岁左右）  身份： 城市腐败网络的核心人物，掌控着巨大的权力和资源

criteria.name: requirement-7
criteria.rubric: The antagonist must be portrayed as scheming and two-faced (老谋深算、表里不一). Source phrase: 老谋深算、表里不一

criteria.name: requirement-8
criteria.rubric: The key supporting character 老李 must be in his 50s and be either an ordinary citizen harmed by corruption or a former minor figure within the system. Source phrase: 老李（50多岁）  身份： 一位因腐败受害的普通市民，或曾是体制内的小人物

criteria.name: requirement-9
criteria.rubric: 老李 must hold key clues relevant to the investigation. Source phrase: 掌握关键线索

criteria.name: requirement-10
criteria.rubric: 老李 must be timid and fearful of trouble while inwardly longing for justice. Source phrase: 他胆小怕事，但内心渴望正义

criteria.name: requirement-11
criteria.rubric: 老李 must eventually, moved by the protagonist, summon the courage to provide help. Source phrase: 最终在主角的感召下，鼓起勇气提供帮助

criteria.name: requirement-12
criteria.rubric: The opening must depict the city's prosperity alongside the chaos of corruption beneath it. Source phrase: 展现城市繁华下的腐败乱象

criteria.name: requirement-13
criteria.rubric: Lin Yu's investigation must be introduced through a specific concrete event. Source phrase: 通过一个具体事件引入林雨的调查

criteria.name: requirement-14
criteria.rubric: Lin Yu must obtain first-hand material for the investigation. Source phrase: 获取第一手资料

criteria.name: requirement-15
criteria.rubric: During the investigation, Lin Yu must encounter key witnesses, including 老李. Source phrase: 遇到老李等关键证人

criteria.name: requirement-17

answer.reasoning:
requirement-1: A: The reply is formatted as a screenplay, with scene headings, action lines, parentheticals and dialogue, and its subject is anti-corruption (拆迁补偿利益输送, arrest of the mayor).
B: The reply is a titled, scene-numbered script with time, location, scene description and dialogue for each act, which fits the requested screenplay about anti-corruption. It is closer to a scene-by-scene treatment than standard screenplay format, so it loses a point.
requirement-2: A: The protagonist is explicitly named 林雨 and listed as 28岁 in the character list.
B: The character list gives the protagonist as 林雨 at 28 years old.
requirement-3: A: Lin Yu is a investigative journalist, described as 性格坚韧正直. Her uprightness is shown in scenes: she pushes the editor to pursue the story, refuses to drop it, and visits 老李 to persuade him.
B: Lin Yu is identified as a young, upright investigative journalist, and her integrity is shown when she refuses the bribe.
requirement-4: A: The family's harm is mentioned twice (father retaliated against for reporting engineering quality problems / for speaking truth), but the first account is cut off mid-sentence and the harm is never dramatized or tied concretely to a corruption incident on screen.
B: Her family's corruption victimhood is stated in the character list and repeated in her dialogue, so it is established as her motive.
requirement-5: A: Lin Yu conducts investigative work: she records audio at the demolition site, goes undercover as a waiter at the club, surveils the mayor's car, submits evidence to prosecutors and exposes it via live stream. Writing is mostly referenced (editorial meetings) rather than shown, so the 'pen' side is thin.
B: She investigates through undercover work, hidden-camera recording, and a newspaper report that is headlined publicly. The investigation is thin, with few concrete investigative steps, but the writing-and-camera exposure route is present.
requirement-6: A: The antagonist 王建军 is 52, mayor and group chairman, and is labelled the network's core, with a phone call showing him directing a land deal. The 'controls vast power' claim is asserted more than shown through a wider network.
B: The antagonist is labelled as a mayor/chairman about 50 and as the core of the corruption network. He never appears on screen, and his control of power and resources is only asserted, so the figure is named but not dramatized.
requirement-7: A: He is shown as cold and threatening (he says he has ways to handle the media and orders the reporter silenced), but there is no public face contrasted with a hidden one, so the two-faced quality is not enacted.
B: Scheming and two-faced behaviour is only asserted as a label in the character list. No scene shows the antagonist acting deceptively or scheming; the only related material is an unseen 'boss' referred to by thugs.
requirement-8: A: 老李 is 56, a retired worker who previously worked in the 建委 (a system role), and he is a displaced compensation-dispute citizen. Both framings are met.
B: 老李 is listed as in his 50s, a former 体制内 minor figure who was harmed by corruption, and is introduced as a worn-looking elderly man who used to work in the relevant department.
requirement-9: A: 老李 provides concrete clues: he says the mayor's company was involved in the 王家巷 project and later offers internal files showing compensation was artificially lowered.
B: 老李 is said to hold key clues and later hands over documents and recordings that are described as proof of the mayor's bribery and embezzlement.
requirement-10: A: He is timid (hushing, saying 'I didn't say anything', 'I have family to protect', refusing), while his inner conflict and sympathy for the demolition families appear in his wife's and his own reactions.
B: Timidity is shown in his dialogue, 'it's no use talking, I don't dare to provoke them'. His inner turmoil appears in the narration. His longing for justice is not voiced by him, only implied by the narration about his inner wavering.
requirement-11: A: After Lin Yu appeals at his door, citing the elderly and children among the displaced families, 老李 says he has decided and offers the internal documents.
B: He is moved by Lin Yu's resolve and then offers help in the park, which satisfies the arc. The turning point itself is reported in one narrated line rather than dramatized, so the change is only partly earned on screen.
requirement-12: A: The opening pairs a CBD skyline with a shanty-town demolition scene where compensation is unfair and thugs disperse protesters, showing corruption beneath prosperity.
B: The opening scene sets a prosperous plaza with towering buildings against workers complaining about unpaid wages and officials pocketing the money, which shows the contrast the brief asks for.
requirement-13: A: The investigation is introduced through a specific event: a demolition-compensation dispute with a visible price gap between districts, which Lin Yu notices and begins to pursue.
B: The investigation starts from a concrete event: the workers' unpaid wages on a stalled project. Lin Yu overhears it and approaches them.
requirement-14: A: She gathers first-hand material covertly: phone audio at the demolition site, undercover recording in the club, surveillance outside the government building, and later 老李's internal documents.
B: She obtains first-hand material by working undercover on the site and recording substandard materials with a hidden camera, plus worker testimony.
requirement-15: A: She meets 老李 at the demolition site and then in a café where he gives clues, plus other displaced residents who react to the broadcast.
B: She meets 老李 in a street restaurant and again in the park, and the workers serve as witnesses in the earlier scenes.
requirement-16: A: No bribe or offer of money or benefit to Lin Yu is depicted. The only related pressure is the editor halting the story on orders from above, which is institutional pressure rather than being bought off.
B: A bribe is offered at her home by black-clad men, who say the boss will pay her to live well, and she refuses. It is present but brief, with no sustained pressure or ambiguity over the offer.
requirement-17: A: Intimidation is enacted: an anonymous call warns her off, a car lunges at her on her way home, and masked men try to stop the live broadcast.
B: Intimidation is dramatised twice: a threatening letter at her door and a car of thugs who threaten to 'not be polite', which escalates the danger.
requirement-18: A: No framing or fabricated charge against Lin Yu appears anywhere in the script.
B: No framing or planted evidence appears. The only false accusation is a suspicious man detaining her at the site, and the workers vouch for her and she is released. That is not a framing crisis.
requirement-19: A: The mayor is arrested on screen (handcuffed in news footage) for serious violations, and the compensation is revised for the displaced families, showing justice.
B: Punishment is stated in one narrated line, 'arrested according to law' and 'other involved persons received penalties', followed by a celebration of justice. The consequence is asserted rather than shown in detail.
requirement-20: A: The reshaping is shown through revised compensation (3500 per square metre), a new mayor promising monitoring mechanisms, and the 老李 family's hopeful reaction.
B: The ending states the city is reshaping order and people are hopeful, with cleaner streets and a celebration crowd. It is brief and asserted rather than dramatized.
requirement-21: A: The ending states the battle is over while the war against corruption never ends, matching the brief's wording.
B: The closing dialogue explicitly says the battle has ended while the anti-corruption war is endless, matching the brief.
requirement-22: A: The closing scene shows a new anonymous tip about the education system, and the final lines look forward, prompting reflection on the future.
B: The final voiceover looks ahead, saying she will keep exposing corruption and that her mission is not over, which gives a reflective note on the future.
development: A: Several beats are enacted with causality: the demolition event, covert recording, witness meeting, intimidation, and the 老李 turn. However, bribery and framing crises are missing, the antagonist's two-faced nature is not shown through behavior, and 老李's turn is compressed into a single door scene.
B: Several beats are enacted: the opening event, covert evidence gathering, encounters with 老李, the bribe, the threat letter and the intimidation, and the reflective ending. However, the framing crisis is missing, the antagonist's scheming never appears through behaviour, and the punishment and renewal are one-line assertions. Causality and rising tension are therefore uneven.
craft: A: Scene progression is mostly clear and characterization is consistent. But the script appends unrequested framing sections ('主题思想', '艺术特色') and extra plot events (live stream, new mayor meeting, award, new tip), and it adds a closing dedication caption, which the brief does not request.
B: The scene order is clear from opening to ending, and Lin Yu and 老李 are consistent. The antagonist is undeveloped, though, and the dialogue is often on-the-nose and generic ('正义一定会战胜邪恶的'). Transitions are functional but abrupt, such as the one-line verdict, and specific original detail is thin.

requirements.requirement: The artifact must be a screenplay (剧本) about anti-corruption (反贪).
requirements.sourceQuote: 请帮我写一个关于反贪的剧本

requirements.requirement: The female protagonist must be named 林雨 and be 28 years old.
requirements.sourceQuote: 女主角：林雨（28岁）

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu must be a young, upright investigative journalist.
requirements.sourceQuote: 一位年轻、正直的调查记者

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu's family must have been harmed by a corruption incident.
requirements.sourceQuote: 她的家人曾因腐败事件受害

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu's task must be to investigate corruption cases in depth and expose the truth through writing and camera work.
requirements.sourceQuote: 深入调查腐败案件，用笔和镜头揭露真相

requirements.requirement: The antagonist must be a mayor or group chairman, about 50 years old, and the core figure of the city's corruption network who controls vast power and resources.
requirements.sourceQuote: 市长/集团董事长（50岁左右）  身份： 城市腐败网络的核心人物，掌控着巨大的权力和资源

requirements.requirement: The antagonist must be portrayed as scheming and two-faced (老谋深算、表里不一).
requirements.sourceQuote: 老谋深算、表里不一

requirements.requirement: The key supporting character 老李 must be in his 50s and be either an ordinary citizen harmed by corruption or a former minor figure within the system.
requirements.sourceQuote: 老李（50多岁）  身份： 一位因腐败受害的普通市民，或曾是体制内的小人物

requirements.requirement: 老李 must hold key clues relevant to the investigation.
requirements.sourceQuote: 掌握关键线索

requirements.requirement: 老李 must be timid and fearful of trouble while inwardly longing for justice.
requirements.sourceQuote: 他胆小怕事，但内心渴望正义

requirements.requirement: 老李 must eventually, moved by the protagonist, summon the courage to provide help.
requirements.sourceQuote: 最终在主角的感召下，鼓起勇气提供帮助

requirements.requirement: The opening must depict the city's prosperity alongside the chaos of corruption beneath it.
requirements.sourceQuote: 展现城市繁华下的腐败乱象

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu's investigation must be introduced through a specific concrete event.
requirements.sourceQuote: 通过一个具体事件引入林雨的调查

requirements.requirement: Lin Yu must obtain first-hand material for the investigation.
requirements.sourceQuote: 获取第一手资料

requirements.requirement: Undercover work and covert filming may be used as methods of obtaining first-hand material; these are examples and not mandatory.
requirements.sourceQuote: 通过卧底、暗访等方式

requirements.requirement: During the investigation, Lin Yu must encounter key witnesses, including 老李.
requirements.sourceQuote: 遇到老李等关键证人

requirements.requirement: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being bought off (被收买).
requirements.sourceQuote: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

requirements.requirement: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being intimidated (被恐吓).
requirements.sourceQuote: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

requirements.requirement: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being framed (被栽赃).
requirements.sourceQuote: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

requirements.requirement: The corrupt offenders must receive their deserved punishment, and justice must be upheld.
requirements.sourceQuote: 腐败分子得到应有的惩罚，正义得以伸张

requirements.requirement: The ending must show the city beginning to reshape its order and the people seeing hope.
requirements.sourceQuote: 城市开始重塑秩序，人民看到了希望

requirements.requirement: The ending must acknowledge that the 'battle' has concluded while the anti-corruption 'war' is endless.
requirements.sourceQuote: 虽然“战役”结束，但反腐的“战争”永无止境

requirements.requirement: The ending must leave the audience with reflection on the future.
requirements.sourceQuote: 留下对未来的思考

brief.development: As a screenplay, judge whether the scenes enact the brief through concrete on-screen events: the opening event that introduces the investigation, Lin Yu's covert gathering of first-hand evidence, the encounters with 老李 and other witnesses, and the bribery, intimidation and framing crises. Each should drive clear causality and rising tension, and 老李's shift from fear to courage must be earned by specific actions and the protagonist's influence. The antagonist's scheming and two-faced nature should appear through behavior, and the punishment of the corrupt and the city's renewal should be shown as results of the preceding conflict, ending with a reflective note about the future.
brief.craft: Judge a coherent screenplay structure with clear scene progression from opening to ending, consistent characterization and voice across Lin Yu, 老李 and the antagonist, and smooth transitions between investigation, confrontation and resolution. The tone should suit a reader or viewer of anti-corruption drama, with original, specific details and no added plot events, promotional elements or framing the commission does not request.

items.rubric: Lin Yu's family must have been harmed by a corruption incident. Source phrase: 她的家人曾因腐败事件受害

items.name: requirement-5
items.rubric: Lin Yu's task must be to investigate corruption cases in depth and expose the truth through writing and camera work. Source phrase: 深入调查腐败案件，用笔和镜头揭露真相

items.name: requirement-6
items.rubric: The antagonist must be a mayor or group chairman, about 50 years old, and the core figure of the city's corruption network who controls vast power and resources. Source phrase: 市长/集团董事长（50岁左右）  身份： 城市腐败网络的核心人物，掌控着巨大的权力和资源

items.name: requirement-7
items.rubric: The antagonist must be portrayed as scheming and two-faced (老谋深算、表里不一). Source phrase: 老谋深算、表里不一

items.name: requirement-8
items.rubric: The key supporting character 老李 must be in his 50s and be either an ordinary citizen harmed by corruption or a former minor figure within the system. Source phrase: 老李（50多岁）  身份： 一位因腐败受害的普通市民，或曾是体制内的小人物

items.name: requirement-9
items.rubric: 老李 must hold key clues relevant to the investigation. Source phrase: 掌握关键线索

items.name: requirement-10
items.rubric: 老李 must be timid and fearful of trouble while inwardly longing for justice. Source phrase: 他胆小怕事，但内心渴望正义

items.name: requirement-11
items.rubric: 老李 must eventually, moved by the protagonist, summon the courage to provide help. Source phrase: 最终在主角的感召下，鼓起勇气提供帮助

items.name: requirement-12
items.rubric: The opening must depict the city's prosperity alongside the chaos of corruption beneath it. Source phrase: 展现城市繁华下的腐败乱象

items.name: requirement-13
items.rubric: Lin Yu's investigation must be introduced through a specific concrete event. Source phrase: 通过一个具体事件引入林雨的调查

items.name: requirement-14
items.rubric: Lin Yu must obtain first-hand material for the investigation. Source phrase: 获取第一手资料

items.name: requirement-15
items.rubric: During the investigation, Lin Yu must encounter key witnesses, including 老李. Source phrase: 遇到老李等关键证人

items.name: requirement-16
items.rubric: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being bought off (被收买). Source phrase: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

items.name: requirement-17
items.rubric: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being intimidated (被恐吓). Source phrase: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

items.name: requirement-18
items.rubric: The story must depict Lin Yu facing a crisis of being framed (被栽赃). Source phrase: 面临着被收买、被恐吓、被栽赃的危机

items.name: requirement-19
items.rubric: The corrupt offenders must receive their deserved punishment, and justice must be upheld. Source phrase: 腐败分子得到应有的惩罚，正义得以伸张

items.name: requirement-20
items.rubric: The ending must show the city beginning to reshape its order and the people seeing hope. Source phrase: 城市开始重塑秩序，人民看到了希望

items.name: requirement-21
items.rubric: The ending must acknowledge that the 'battle' has concluded while the anti-corruption 'war' is endless. Source phrase: 虽然“战役”结束，但反腐的“战争”永无止境

items.name: requirement-22
items.rubric: The ending must leave the audience with reflection on the future. Source phrase: 留下对未来的思考

items.name: development
items.rubric: As a screenplay, judge whether the scenes enact the brief through concrete on-screen events: the opening event that introduces the investigation, Lin Yu's covert gathering of first-hand evidence, the encounters with 老李 and other witnesses, and the bribery, intimidation and framing crises. Each should drive clear causality and rising tension, and 老李's shift from fear to courage must be earned by specific actions and the protagonist's influence. The antagonist's scheming and two-faced nature should appear through behavior, and the punishment of the corrupt and the city's renewal should be shown as results of the preceding conflict, ending with a reflective note about the future.

items.name: craft
items.rubric: Judge a coherent screenplay structure with clear scene progression from opening to ending, consistent characterization and voice across Lin Yu, 老李 and the antagonist, and smooth transitions between investigation, confrontation and resolution. The tone should suit a reader or viewer of anti-corruption drama, with original, specific details and no added plot events, promotional elements or framing the commission does not request.
